events.title: HTML invented
events.summary: Tim Berners-Lee invented [HTML] in 1991 at CERN — a markup language of tags for linking documents on the World Wide Web.
events.about:
[HTML] wraps text in elements like ``, `

`, and `

` so browsers know structure and hyperlinks. Berners-Lee paired it with [HTTP] and URLs; every web page, email template, and SPA still renders [HTML] (or generates it). Example: `Read more` turns text into a clickable navigation link.

narrative.whyChosen: [HTML] was the document format that made the web browsable, not just transferable files.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the universal presentation layer of the internet — later extended by [CSS] and JavaScript.
narrative.problemSolved: Scientists at CERN needed a simple way to write and link research documents across machines.
